decisions.decision: AR0144 stereo capture resolution changed from 2560x720 to 1600x600 (800x600 per eye)
decisions.rationale: 2560x720 confirmed persistently frozen (byte-identical frames) via raw ffmpeg testing AND direct inspection of a real episode's 300 recorded frames -- confirmed a real, not-our-code bug. Exhausted all fixes: process cleanup, VDCAssistant restart, camera replug, full OS reboot, and macOS's legacy-camera-plugins-without-sw-camera-indication recovery-mode system override -- none restored 2560x720. 1600x600 confirmed live/stable (20+ consecutive frames with genuine non-zero diffs) and is the best available resolution (next mode up jumps straight to the broken 2560x720; intermediate 1280x480/1280x712 are single-lens crops, not stereo pairs).

decisions.decision: Stereo calibration required 30 views with deliberately varied angle/position/distance to converge
decisions.rationale: First 2-3 attempts (15 views each, low variety) produced inconsistent baseline (T) estimates between independent runs (75mm vs 53mm, a 30% swing) despite low-ish reprojection error -- a red flag that reprojection error alone doesn't guarantee a trustworthy calibration. 30 views with real angle/position/distance variety converged: baseline agreed to within 0.6% between the last two attempts, reprojection error dropped to 1.79px, distortion coefficients shrank monotonically toward physically sane values.

decisions.decision: Built 3 new hardware-debugging/calibration tools this session, committed to control/: preview_checkerboard.py, calibrate_with_preview.py, tune_execution_hz.py
decisions.rationale: The production stereo_calibration.py's capture loop is headless (input()-prompt, no visual feedback) -- these tools add live preview to make manual calibration/tuning practical. tune_execution_hz.py exercises run_episode()'s real interpolation code against a scripted multi-joint sweep without needing the Colab bridge, used to tune --execution-hz from 20.0 to 100.0.
